'''Jeremy LaMere''' was a finalist at the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]]. The packet lists the name as "Jeremy Lamere." LaMere qualified through Tatooine Salt Lake City from Phoenix, Arizona.<ref name="pkt">[https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf 1998 World Championship packet], Decipher / Kendrick Summers (20 November 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195330/https://blog.categoryonegames.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/1998-World-Championship.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> LaMere won the [[1997 Tatooine Regionals (Phoenix)]], a qualifier for the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]].<ref name="dec97q">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/regionalsandopens.html 1997 Regionals and Open Events], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990503132332/http://search.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/regionalsandopens.html Internet Archive]</ref>

The 36-player event was hosted by [[William Schmidt]], and LaMere beat Brandon Allen in the final.<ref name="decsq-schmidtwilliam">[http://www.decipher.com/volunteers/squadrons/players/schmidtwilliam.html Star Wars CCG Squadrons: Gold 18 profile], decipher.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000607001535/http://decipher.com:80/volunteers/squadrons/players/schmidtwilliam.html Internet Archive]</ref>
